summary:
ATLAS is a free, open-source Mars exploration and survival-planning platform developed by Team Protikriti for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by transforming scattered NASA scientific data into interactive tools that support safer human exploration of Mars.

ATLAS features two integrated modes. Map Mode combines real NASA imagery, 3D terrain, radiation, weather, buried water ice, and mineral data into an interactive Martian map. Its Marswalk planner evaluates terrain slopes, identifies hazards, calculates safe return routes, and provides GO/NO-GO mission assessments. Astronauts can also explore rover panoramas and simulate surface exploration.

Mission Mode challenges users to manage a four-person crew through 525 Martian sols, making critical decisions about supplies, habitats, resources, and emergencies. Every decision has consequences, and mission reports help users learn from failures.

Powered by tested scientific calculations, offline capabilities, and evidence-based AI, ATLAS provides an accessible environment for exploring, planning, and understanding the challenges of surviving on Mars.
details:
ATLAS — Interplanetary Survival Guide for Mars

1. Project Overview

ATLAS is a free, open-source web application developed by Team Protikriti to help future Mars explorers plan safer surface missions and understand the challenges of surviving on another planet.

Our project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 problem, "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map," by integrating publicly available NASA scientific datasets into a unified, interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform.

On Mars, astronauts will face dangerous terrain, limited resources, extreme environmental conditions, and communication delays with Earth. Although NASA has collected enormous amounts of Martian data, much of this information is distributed across different missions and databases.

ATLAS brings these resources together through two complementary experiences: Map Mode and Mission Mode.

Explore ATLAS and learn more about our project:

Live Application: https://atlas-mars.vercel.app/

Detailed Project Demonstration (240 seconds): https://youtu.be/cV5MpehaCBc

Full Project Details, Source Code, and Technical Documentation: https://github.com/AhsanulHoque22/Nasa-Space-Apps-Challenge-2026-Team-Protikriti

2. How ATLAS Works

Map Mode: Scientific Exploration and Navigation

Map Mode provides an interactive 3D representation of Mars using CesiumJS and real planetary imagery and elevation data from NASA's HiRISE, CTX, MOLA, Mars Trek, and USGS terrain models.

Users can click on locations to generate scientific site reports containing information about terrain, sunlight, buried water ice, ground firmness, mineral composition, surface radiation, and nearby geographical landmarks.

Our Marswalk Planner allows users to design exploration routes in Jezero and Gale craters. It evaluates terrain slopes against a 15-degree threshold, assesses potential hazards, and calculates whether astronauts can return to their habitat within the available EVA time budget.

The system generates GO/NO-GO assessments, identifies unsafe route segments, and explains how safety limits are exceeded. Users can mark obstacles and explore alternative routes while understanding the additional time and distance required.

We tested the slope-assessment rule against 556 real Perseverance rover drive legs to evaluate its behavior against recorded Martian traverses.

Map Mode also includes:

  • An EVA console for monitoring oxygen, battery, slopes, return-time margins, and safety alerts.
  • Exploration-zone rankings covering 30 NASA candidate human landing zones.
  • More than 2,000 rover observation locations with 360-degree panoramas assembled from NASA Navcam imagery.
  • Experimental terrain classification using a Random Forest model trained on NASA's AI4Mars dataset.
  • Simulated surface exploration with Martian gravity and environmental conditions based on Curiosity and Perseverance weather observations.
  • Pressurized rover exploration of scientific destinations.
  • Earth–Mars communication-delay calculations using JPL planetary positions.
  • Offline functionality for supported exploration tools.

Mission Mode: A 525-Sol Survival Simulation

Mission Mode transforms scientific planning into an interactive survival experience based on NASA's Design Reference Architecture 5.0.

Users manage a crew of four astronauts throughout a simulated 525-sol expedition.

They must select mission supplies, choose landing zones, establish habitats, produce food and water, survive dust storms, explore caves, manage equipment failures, and prepare for the return journey.

Every decision affects subsequent mission events.

For example, selecting insufficient power reactors before launch can cause a greenhouse power failure months later, putting the mission's food supply at risk.

Each attempt produces a mission report that helps users understand what went wrong, trace the consequences of earlier decisions, revise their strategy, and try again.

This allows users to experience the complexity of Mars mission planning without putting real lives at risk.

3. Technology and Development

ATLAS is a browser-based application that combines interactive 3D visualization, scientific data processing, simulation systems, and AI-assisted explanations.

Our primary technologies and resources include:

  • CesiumJS for interactive 3D planetary visualization.
  • NASA HiRISE, CTX, and MOLA imagery and elevation data.
  • NASA Mars Trek and USGS planetary terrain models.
  • SWIM 2.0 for subsurface water-ice information.
  • THEMIS and CRISM for surface and mineral observations.
  • Curiosity RAD for radiation measurements.
  • REMS and MEDA for Martian weather observations.
  • NASA Navcam imagery for rover panoramas.
  • AI4Mars and Random Forest machine learning for experimental terrain classification.
  • JPL planetary-position data for Earth–Mars communication-delay calculations.
  • Claude Haiku 5.5 for the Ask ATLAS scientific explainer.

Scientific calculations are implemented through deterministic application code, supported by more than 1,000 automated tests.

Our AI assistant explains results using application-provided information, cites supporting facts, and checks numerical statements against available data. It does not independently calculate scientific values.

The application is open source under the Apache-2.0 license.

4. Creativity and Innovation

ATLAS goes beyond displaying a map of Mars.

Its primary innovation is integrating multiple scientific datasets with mission-planning calculations and interactive survival simulations.

Rather than simply showing where astronauts could travel, ATLAS helps users understand whether a proposed journey is feasible, what hazards might affect it, and whether the crew can return safely.

The Marswalk Planner checks return feasibility from every route point instead of only evaluating the distance to the destination.

Mission Mode introduces another dimension by connecting early planning decisions to consequences that may emerge months later.

We also distinguish between verified scientific calculations and experimental AI predictions, ensuring that uncertain terrain-classification results are not used for safety-critical route decisions.

Together, these features create an interactive environment where users can explore Mars, evaluate risks, and understand why successful missions require careful planning.

5. Intended Impact and Benefits

ATLAS aims to make planetary exploration more accessible, understandable, and engaging.

For students and educators, it provides an interactive way to learn about Martian geography, planetary science, resource management, and human space exploration.

For researchers and mission designers, it demonstrates how different planetary datasets can be integrated into exploratory planning workflows.

For the general public, it transforms complex scientific information into a practical and engaging experience.

Most importantly, ATLAS encourages evidence-based decision-making by making assumptions, limitations, and scientific sources visible.

It is an educational and research prototype, not certified astronaut-navigation software.

6. Challenges and Design Considerations

During development, we considered several important challenges:

  • Integrating datasets from different NASA missions with varying resolutions, coordinate systems, and coverage.
  • Handling terrain uncertainty, particularly where elevation maps cannot resolve smaller obstacles.
  • Evaluating route safety while considering both outbound travel and the return journey.
  • Combining resource constraints and environmental hazards in a consistent simulation.
  • Building useful offline functionality for environments with limited connectivity.
  • Keeping scientific calculations separate from AI-generated explanations.
  • Communicating uncertainty rather than presenting estimates as verified measurements.

We addressed these challenges through modular data integration, transparent assumptions, automated testing, and explicit reporting of data limitations.

7. Future Development

We plan to improve ATLAS by extending route analysis to 1-meter HiRISE terrain where available, incorporating NASA EVA mobility research, expanding high-resolution geographic coverage, and validating more mission-simulation assumptions.

We also aim to improve terrain-classification accuracy and conduct practical evaluations with analog astronaut crews.

8. Conclusion

Real missions to Mars require enormous resources and involve serious human risks.

ATLAS provides a virtual environment where exploration plans can be studied, tested, and improved before similar decisions must be made in reality.

By combining NASA scientific datasets, interactive planetary mapping, tested calculations, and survival simulations, we hope to make Mars exploration more accessible while demonstrating the importance of thoughtful, science-based mission planning.

Our vision is simple: explore Mars, plan smarter, and learn from mistakes before they become real emergencies.

Live Project: https://atlas-mars.vercel.app/
